chunks: And from him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Wuhayb ibn Ḥafṣ, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “If there were a river at the door of one of your houses, and he were to bathe in it five times every day, would any filth remain on his body?” We said: “No.” He said: “Then indeed the likeness of salat is like that of a flowing river: whenever he performs a salat, it expiates the sins committed between them.”

key_terms.الدَّرَنِ: filth or grime, symbolizing impurities being removed
key_terms.الذُّنُوبِ: sins committed between one salat and the next
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the act of worship likened to a cleansing river
key_terms.الْجَارِي: flowing, describing the river’s continuous movement and cleansing quality
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, the speaker of the parable
key_terms.كَفَّرَتْ: it expiated or erased, referring to the removal of sins
key_terms.نَهَرٌ: a river, used as the central image of repeated purification

ai.seo_question: How do the five daily salat remove sins in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith compares the cleansing effect of the five daily salat to a flowing river in which a person bathes repeatedly. It teaches that regular salat purifies a believer from sins occurring between the prayers and highlights the great spiritual virtue of maintaining them consistently.
